payload.stem: A least-squares regression line for predicting the number of cups of hot chocolate sold from the temperature, in degrees Celsius is $\hat y = 94.5 - 3.84x$, based on data for which $x$ ranges from $0$ to $15$, with $r = -0.91$. A researcher uses the line to predict number of cups when $x = 34$. Which of the following statements about the prediction is correct?

options.text: The prediction of $-36.1$ is reliable, because the correlation of $0.91$ is close to $1$.
options.why: A strong correlation within the range of the data does not make predictions outside that range reliable.

options.text: The prediction of $-36.1$ is an extrapolation, because $34$ is outside the range of the data, so the linear pattern may not continue and the prediction may be unreliable.
options.why: Predictions for values of the explanatory variable outside the range of the data assume that the linear pattern continues, which the data cannot confirm.

options.text: The prediction of $-36.1$ is reliable, because the line is the least-squares line, which has the smallest sum of squared residuals.
options.why: The least-squares property describes the fit to the observed data, not the behavior of the relationship outside the data.

options.text: The prediction cannot be made, because a regression line can only be used for the values of $x$ that appear in the data set.
options.why: A prediction can be calculated for any value of $x$; the issue is that it is unreliable outside the range of the data.

The correct answer is The prediction of $46.1$ is an extrapolation, because $36$ is outside the range of the data, so the linear pattern may not continue and the prediction may be unreliable.. Predictions for values of the explanatory variable outside the range of the data assume that the linear pattern continues, which the data cannot confirm.
The prediction of $46.1$ is reliable, because the line is the least-squares line, which has the smallest sum of squared residuals. is incorrect: The least-squares property describes the fit to the observed data, not the behavior of the relationship outside the data.
The prediction cannot be made, because a regression line can only be used for the values of $x$ that appear in the data set. is incorrect: A prediction can be calculated for any value of $x$; the issue is that it is unreliable outside the range of the data.
The prediction of $46.1$ is reliable, because the correlation of $0.91$ is close to $1$. is incorrect: A strong correlation within the range of the data does not make predictions outside that range reliable.

payload.stem: A least-squares regression line for predicting the number of cups of hot chocolate sold from the temperature, in degrees Celsius is $\hat y = 95.4 - 3.62x$, based on data for which $x$ ranges from $0$ to $15$, with $r = -0.88$. A researcher uses the line to predict number of cups when $x = 30$. Which of the following statements about the prediction is correct?

options.text: The prediction of $-13.2$ is reliable, because the line is the least-squares line, which has the smallest sum of squared residuals.
options.why: The least-squares property describes the fit to the observed data, not the behavior of the relationship outside the data.

options.text: The prediction of $-13.2$ is an extrapolation, because $30$ is outside the range of the data, so the linear pattern may not continue and the prediction may be unreliable.
options.why: Predictions for values of the explanatory variable outside the range of the data assume that the linear pattern continues, which the data cannot confirm.

options.text: The prediction cannot be made, because a regression line can only be used for the values of $x$ that appear in the data set.
options.why: A prediction can be calculated for any value of $x$; the issue is that it is unreliable outside the range of the data.

options.text: The prediction of $-13.2$ is reliable, because the correlation of $0.88$ is close to $1$.
options.why: A strong correlation within the range of the data does not make predictions outside that range reliable.
